title: How to plan an office pantry vending service
excerpt: Compare staff-paid and employer-subsidised pantry options, agree a service plan and set measures for an office pilot.
opening: Start with the employees the pantry needs to serve. Staff on a late shift may have different needs from a team that works near a canteen at lunchtime. Ask for the products, price points and service windows that solve the biggest gap, then choose a payment arrangement your team can administer.
checklist: Record headcount by shift and typical on-site days. Note which groups have limited access to other food and drinks.
Collect preferences for snacks, beverages, dietary needs and pricing. Agree what information should appear on product labels or selections.
Compare staff-paid, partial subsidy and employer-funded options. Ask what the machine can support, what reporting is available and how reconciliation works.
If subsidising, agree which products qualify, who can use the subsidy, how limits work and who reviews spending. Test the payment flow before launch.
Assign responsibilities for refills, cleaning, faults, refunds and stock changes. Give employees a clear contact for issues.
Review availability during each shift, complaints, use and budget after the pilot. Decide whether to adjust the assortment, subsidy or refill schedule.
close: Send the operator your headcount, work pattern, location photos and preferred funding model. A single page is enough for a first proposal.
